Coined by Johan Galtung: violence built into social structures without an explicit individual assailant.

questions.chapter_title: Peace Psychology: Understanding the Human Mind in Conflict and Reconciliation
questions.question: [Workbook Q13] According to the Society for the Study of Peace, Conflict, and Violence (2006), the goals of Peace Psychology are ________.

options.D: To understand psychological causes of conflict, apply psychological...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q13): To understand psychological causes of conflict, apply psychological knowledge to reduce violence, and promote social justice and sustainable peace. Official mandate of APA Division 48.

questions.chapter_title: Peace Psychology: Understanding the Human Mind in Conflict and Reconciliation
questions.question: [Workbook Q14] The vision of peace psychologists is ________.

options.B: A world where human disputes are addressed through non-violent dial...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q14): A world where human disputes are addressed through non-violent dialogue, empathy, reconciliation, and structural justice. Transforming adversarial dynamics into collaborative co-existence.

questions.chapter_title: Peace Psychology: Understanding the Human Mind in Conflict and Reconciliation
questions.question: [Workbook Q15] Briefly outline the aims of Peace Psychology: (i), (ii), (iii), (iv), (v), (vi).
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q15): (i) Analyzing psychological roots of hatred, dehumanization, and intergroup bias. (ii) Mitigating trauma and PTSD in post-war populations. (iii) Fostering intergroup contact and empathy across historical divides. (iv) Promoting non-violent conflict resolution skills in schools and communities. (v) Challenging structural and cultural violence. (vi) Supporting truth, healing, and reconciliation processes.. Comprehensive clinical and social peace psychology agenda.

questions.chapter_title: Peace Psychology: Understanding the Human Mind in Conflict and Reconciliation
questions.question: [Workbook Q16] Who proposed the concepts of positive peace and negative peace?
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q16): Johan Galtung (1964, 1969). Foundational dichotomy of international peace research.

questions.chapter_title: Peace Psychology: Understanding the Human Mind in Conflict and Reconciliation
questions.question: [Workbook Q17] What is positive peace?

options.B: The presence of social justice, equality, institutional fairness, h...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q17): The presence of social justice, equality, institutional fairness, human rights, and the total absence of both direct and structural violence.. Sustainable flourishing of society.

questions.chapter_title: Peace Psychology: Understanding the Human Mind in Conflict and Reconciliation
questions.question: [Workbook Q18] What is negative peace?

options.B: The mere absence of direct, active physical violence or war, even w...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q18): The mere absence of direct, active physical violence or war, even while underlying injustices, oppression, and fear persist.. Unstable ceasefires without systemic justice.

questions.chapter_title: Legal Framework for Social Justice and Conflict Resolution in Nigeria
questions.question: [Workbook Q1] The major legal instrument for the defence of human rights in Nigeria derives from the ________.

options.B: 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q1): 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Chapter IV: Fundamental Rights). Sections 33 to 44 guarantee fundamental human rights (Right to life, dignity, personal liberty, fair hearing, etc.).

questions.chapter_title: Legal Framework for Social Justice and Conflict Resolution in Nigeria
questions.question: [Workbook Q2] The Universal Declaration of Human Rights to which Nigeria is a signatory is an example of a ________.

options.D: Multilateral International Human Rights Treaty / Global Normative I...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q2): Multilateral International Human Rights Treaty / Global Normative Instrument. Adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in Paris on 10 December 1948.

questions.chapter_title: Legal Framework for Social Justice and Conflict Resolution in Nigeria
questions.question: [Workbook Q3] ________ establishes the legal framework and other mechanisms to hold government accountable in the event they violate human rights.
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q3): Constitutionalism (The Rule of Law and Judicial Review). Limits arbitrary government power through independent courts.

questions.chapter_title: Legal Framework for Social Justice and Conflict Resolution in Nigeria
questions.question: [Workbook Q4] Legal framework can be viewed from ________ and ________ dimensions.
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q4): Substantive (statutory laws, rights, doctrines) and Procedural / Institutional (courts, enforcement agencies, rules of litigation). Two interdependent pillars of any jurisprudence system.

questions.chapter_title: Legal Framework for Social Justice and Conflict Resolution in Nigeria
questions.question: [Workbook Q5] ________ provides a basis for enforcing law and policies that promote order, justice and fairness.
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q5): The Legal Framework / The Constitution. Supreme law of the land from which all institutional legitimacy derives (Section 1(1) & 1(3)).

questions.chapter_title: Legal Framework for Social Justice and Conflict Resolution in Nigeria
questions.question: [Workbook Q6] Legal framework can best be conceptualized as ________.

options.B: A coherent system of interrelated laws, judicial precedents, consti...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q6): A coherent system of interrelated laws, judicial precedents, constitutional principles, and regulatory institutions that govern societal behavior and arbitrate disputes. The bedrock of modern democratic governance.

questions.chapter_title: Legal Framework for Social Justice and Conflict Resolution in Nigeria
questions.question: [Workbook Q7] According to FasterCapital (2024), a legal framework provides ________.

options.C: Legal predictability, contractual certainty, protection of property...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q7): Legal predictability, contractual certainty, protection of property rights, and institutional checks and balances. Essential for conflict resolution and socio-economic investment.

questions.chapter_title: Legal Framework for Social Justice and Conflict Resolution in Nigeria
questions.question: [Workbook Q8] The growth of Nigeria's legal system has been linked to ________.
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q8): English Common Law tradition, Islamic (Sharia) Law, and Indigenous Customary Law (the tripartite legal heritage). Pluralistic nature of Nigerian jurisprudence.

questions.chapter_title: Legal Framework for Social Justice and Conflict Resolution in Nigeria
questions.question: [Workbook Q9] Human rights issues have been a subject for debate in ________ and ________ circles since the ________ and ________ until the present democratic government.
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q9): academic and civil society / political; colonial era and military regimes. Long struggles against authoritarian decrees to achieve constitutional democracy.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q1] Community policing differs significantly from conventional policing approaches that stress coercive authority, ________, and ________.

options.A: Reactive incident response, state-centric hierarchy, and bureaucrat...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q1): Reactive incident response, state-centric hierarchy, and bureaucratic isolation. Shift from authoritarian policing to democratic, service-oriented problem-solving.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q2] ________ encourages cooperation between law enforcement officers and the communities they serve.
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q2): Community Policing. Pioneered by Sir Robert Peel: 'The police are the public and the public are the police.'

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q3] The notion of community policing holds that security is a shared duty of the state, residents, community leaders, civil society groups, and ________.

options.A: Traditional institutions / Local vigilante formations / Private bus...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q3): Traditional institutions / Local vigilante formations / Private business sector. Multi-stakeholder security governance model.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q4] Community policing seeks to identify and address the root causes of crime and social unrest via ________.

options.D: Proactive problem-solving, intelligence-led collaboration, and gras...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q4): Proactive problem-solving, intelligence-led collaboration, and grassroots dialogue. Addressing underlying socio-economic drivers rather than only reacting after crimes occur.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q5] Nigeria's diverse ________ and ________ backgrounds can lead to ________ tensions and localized conflicts that traditional enforcement techniques struggle to address effectively.
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q5): ethnic and religious; sectarian / communal. Cultural diversity requires culturally nuanced dispute resolution.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q6] Traditional enforcement is particularly problematic in ________ and ________ where distrust in government institutions endures.

options.A: Rural agrarian communities and informal urban slums / marginalized ...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q6): Rural agrarian communities and informal urban slums / marginalized settlements. Deep historical suspicion of armed police tactical units.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q7] Community policing is increasingly recognised as a strategic technique for connecting institutions with the ________ they serve.
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q7): Grassroots citizens (local communities). Bridges the legitimacy gap between law enforcement and citizens.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q8] Kenku and Umar (2025) argue that ________.

options.C: Community policing provides the vital architecture for rebuilding p...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q8): Community policing provides the vital architecture for rebuilding public confidence in Nigeria's internal security apparatus. Recent academic verification of policing reforms.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q9] According to Aremu et al. (2024), constant involvement between police officers and community people improved ________, ________, and ________, and aided in the resolution of communal conflicts in urban environments.

options.B: Mutual trust, actionable intelligence sharing, and timely dispute m...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q9): Mutual trust, actionable intelligence sharing, and timely dispute mediation. Empirical study on urban community policing in Nigeria.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q10] According to Aremu et al. (2024), community policing can improve security governance by encouraging ________ and ________ for maintaining peace and order.
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q10): Shared ownership and civic co-responsibility. Citizens shift from passive observers to active security partners.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q11] Community policing projects help to create ________.

options.B: Safe spaces and structured community-police consultative forums

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q11): Safe spaces and structured community-police consultative forums. Regular platforms for joint safety planning.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q12] Community policing creates platforms for conversation and collaboration, allowing ________, ________, and ________ to actively participate in identifying potential conflict.

options.B: Youth leaders, women groups, and traditional elders / religious fig...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q12): Youth leaders, women groups, and traditional elders / religious figures. Inclusive community representation.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q13] In restive environments, collaborative community policing initiatives can serve as ________ and prevent disagreements from escalating into ________.
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q13): Early warning and de-escalation buffers; violent communal warfare / bloodshed. Preventing skirmishes from turning into full-scale communal clashes.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q14] In Kogi State, cooperative community-based security measures including ________, ________, and ________ have improved public safety and strengthened local responses to criminal activity.

options.B: Joint community vigilante patrols, hunter associations integration,...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q14): Joint community vigilante patrols, hunter associations integration, and local intelligence taskforces. Case study of hybrid sub-national security collaboration.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q15] In Anambra State, community policing measures were found to have ________ in ________ and resulted in improved local safety.
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q15): curbed armed robbery and kidnapping; commercial trading hubs and transit towns. Anambra Vigilante Group (AVG) and neighborhood watch partnership.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q16] Community policing in Nigeria faces two types of challenges namely ________ and ________.
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q16): Internal/Structural challenges and External/Societal challenges. Systemic institutional and socio-political impediments.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q17] Some of the major challenges of community policing in Nigeria are ________.

options.D: Inadequate funding and modern logistics, deep historical public dis...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q17): Inadequate funding and modern logistics, deep historical public distrust from police brutality, political interference by state governors, and poor welfare of personnel. Cripples implementation fidelity across state commands.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q18] What is a community?

options.C: A social unit or group of people living within a shared geographica...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q18): A social unit or group of people living within a shared geographical area or bound by common interests, traditions, cultural identity, and mutual interdependence.. Sociological definition combining geography, shared values, and mutual ties.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q19] Communities are more than just physical locations; they are complex social systems marked by ________.

options.D: Interconnected kinship networks, shared values, historical memories...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q19): Interconnected kinship networks, shared values, historical memories, and social norms. Relational understanding of community.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q20] Communities are critical forums for ________ and ________, where collective norms impact conduct and disagreements are typically addressed using culturally established procedures such as ________ and ________.
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q20): Socialization and collective identity; elder conciliation and traditional customary arbitration. Endogenous African conflict resolution mechanisms.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q21] What is policing?

options.D: The organized social function of maintaining public order, enforcin...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q21): The organized social function of maintaining public order, enforcing laws, preventing and detecting crime, and protecting lives and property in a society.. Distinction between the police as an institution and policing as a broad societal function.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q22] The primary responsibilities of the police include the following: ________, ________, and ________.

options.B: Protection of life and property, preservation of public law and ord...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q22): Protection of life and property, preservation of public law and order, and apprehension and prosecution of offenders. Statutory duties under Section 4 of the Nigeria Police Act.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q23] Contemporary policing and maintaining order necessitates the involvement of a wide range of stakeholders, including ________.

options.A: Community elders, youth councils, vigilante networks, civil society...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q23): Community elders, youth councils, vigilante networks, civil society organizations, and private security companies. Pluralization of contemporary security architecture.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q24] Adeyemi and Bamidele (2024) posit that contemporary policing ________.

options.A: Must transition from an antagonistic military-era force into a tran...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q24): Must transition from an antagonistic military-era force into a transparent, rights-respecting civilian service accountable to the people. Democratization of policing imperatives.

questions.chapter_title: Community Policing: Evolution and Imperatives for Conflict Resolution
questions.question: [Workbook Q25] What is community policing?

options.B: A philosophy and organizational strategy that promotes proactive pa...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q25): A philosophy and organizational strategy that promotes proactive partnership between law enforcement and citizens to solve crime, fear of crime, and neighborhood social disorders.. Standard criminological definition.

questions.chapter_title: Conflict Early Warning and Early Response Systems
questions.question: [Workbook Q1] ________ were originally created as crucial frameworks for conflict prevention.
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q1): Conflict Early Warning Systems (CEWS). Designed to detect tensions before violence erupts.

questions.chapter_title: Conflict Early Warning and Early Response Systems
questions.question: [Workbook Q2] ________ is a structured approach that entails gathering and examining data to recognize possible threats prior to their emergence.
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q2): Early Warning. Information-driven preventive mechanism.

questions.chapter_title: Conflict Early Warning and Early Response Systems
questions.question: [Workbook Q3] ________ defines early warning as a tool that alerts decision makers to the potential outbreak, escalation and resurgence of violent conflict.

options.D: The Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q3): The Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) / United Nations. International diplomatic definition.

questions.chapter_title: Conflict Early Warning and Early Response Systems
questions.question: [Workbook Q4] ________ involves actions taken immediately after a threat is recognized, focused on managing, resolving, or preventing violence or disaster.
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q4): Early Response. Connecting warning data to proactive interventions.

questions.chapter_title: Conflict Early Warning and Early Response Systems
questions.question: [Workbook Q5] Early response measures might include ________.

options.A: Preventive diplomacy, mediation deployment, police peace patrols, p...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q5): Preventive diplomacy, mediation deployment, police peace patrols, public dialogue, and humanitarian pre-positioning. Diverse political, judicial, and tactical response actions.

questions.chapter_title: Conflict Early Warning and Early Response Systems
questions.question: [Workbook Q6] What is risk knowledge?

options.D: The comprehensive understanding of hazards, vulnerabilities, and co...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q6): The comprehensive understanding of hazards, vulnerabilities, and community exposure to conflict or disaster dynamics within a given territory.. Baseline empirical foundation for warning systems.

questions.chapter_title: Conflict Early Warning and Early Response Systems
questions.question: [Workbook Q7] What are the components of risk knowledge?

options.B: Hazard identification, vulnerability assessment, capacity analysis,...

questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q7): Hazard identification, vulnerability assessment, capacity analysis, and exposure mapping. The 4 core elements of risk assessment.

questions.chapter_title: Conflict Early Warning and Early Response Systems
questions.question: [Workbook Q8] ________ entails systematic observation to detect early signs of emerging threats and the generation of warnings when predefined thresholds are approached or exceeded.
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q8): Monitoring and Warning Service (Threat Surveillance). Second pillar of early warning systems.

questions.question: [Workbook Q9] ________ ensures that warnings reach decision-makers, response actors, and at-risk populations in time for action to be taken.

questions.chapter_title: Conflict Early Warning and Early Response Systems
questions.question: [Workbook Q12] Briefly explain the following Operational Levels of early warning systems: (i) Top-down systems, (ii) Bottom-up systems, (iii) Hybrid approaches; and the following Methodologies: (iv) Indicator-based, (v) Predictive machine learning, (vi) Event-based surveillance.
questions.explanation: Official CA Workbook Solution (Review Q12): (i) Top-down: State-centric, intelligence-driven, and managed by national security agencies. (ii) Bottom-up: Grassroots, community-based monitoring by citizens and local NGOs. (iii) Hybrid: Blends satellite/state data with grassroots reporting (e.g. WANEP/ECOWARN). (iv) Indicator-based: Tracks structured qualitative/quantitative indices (hate speech index, arms prices). (v) Predictive ML: Uses big data and machine learning to forecast conflict probability. (vi) Event-based: Monitors sudden trigger incidents in real time.. Comprehensive typology of modern early warning architectures.
